newsitem.title: USA: Energy Under Secretary Grumbly resigns. [CORRECTED 23:59 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Energy Under Secretary Grumbly resigns. [CORRECTED 23:59 GMT]

text.p: The head of the Energy Department's multibillion-dollar program to clean up contaminated nuclear weapons sites will resign on April 4 (corrects from Friday) to join private industry, the department said Monday.

Under Secretary Thomas Grumbly, the department's third highest ranking official, will become an executive vice president of ICF Kaiser International Inc. and president of the engineering, construction and environmental cleanup firm's federal programs group. The company is based in Fairfax, Va.
Grumbly joined the Energy Department in June 1993 as an assistant secretary for environmental management and became an under secretary in May 1996.

"He transformed the Environmental Management program from a bureaucracy focused on studying problems to one that is accomplishing hundreds of on-the-ground cleanup projects at former weapons sites around the country," Energy Secretary Federico Pena said in a statement.
Grumbly also was involved in efforts to regain control of U.S. nuclear fuel from foreign research reactors to keep bomb-grade material out of unauthorized hands.
